title: Adaptive multi-GPU scheduler for prefill/decode coordination and NCCL overlap
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement an adaptive scheduler that coordinates tensor and pipeline parallel stages to maximize NCCL overlap during prefill and decode phases. Goal is to reduce end-to-end latency for batched streaming workloads while maintaining throughput and stability across mixed sequence-length distributions.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can switch between prefill-optimized and decode-optimized modes at runtime without restarting workers
Measured NCCL all-reduce overlap increases by >=20% on average for 8xA100 setup on our benchmark suite
99th percentile token latency reduced by at least 15% for streaming generation workloads in the defined benchmark
No regressions in throughput (tokens/sec) for large-batch offline workloads (within 5%)
Automated tests covering coordination logic and a deterministic simulation harness added to CI
tasks: Prototype controller that tracks prefill vs decode traffic and toggles scheduling heuristics
Integrate NCCL timeline hooks to surface overlap metrics to telemetry
Add kernel-selection hints per-stage to runtime for attention and matmul ops
Implement soft handoff between tensor and pipeline parallel placement for small-sequence low-latency cases
Run performance sweep across sequence-length distributions and report results
Create canary rollout config for Dedicated clusters and guardrails for Private deployments
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting — aligned on metrics (NCCL overlap, p99 token latency, throughput). Rohan to lead implementation; Chris to own kernel hints.
2026-02-20: Prototype controller submitted (WIP) in branch feat/mgpu-adaptive-scheduler; basic heuristic: if decode_ratio > 0.6, prefer decode-optimized scheduling.
2026-02-24: Telemetry hooks added to runtime to emit per-stage NCCL start/end timestamps (PR #3124). Need to ensure low overhead in hot path.
2026-02-26: Early benchmarks on 4xA100 show NCCL overlap improvement ~9% for streaming with mixed sequences; decode p99 improved by 8% — on track but below target.
2026-03-01: Added kernel-selection hints for FlashAttention vs standard attention depending on token length distribution; microbenchmarks show 5-12% per-op improvement for short sequences.

2026-03-03: Integration tests added to CI simulation harness (deterministic replay of prefill/decode interleavings). Findings: edge-case when background KV-cache eviction triggers extra NCCL ops. Investigating mitigation.
decisions: Use a controller-based approach (centralized in the scheduler service) to compute scheduling policy and broadcast lightweight hints to workers rather than full leader migration.
Prefer non-blocking NCCL semantics where supported and fall back to legacy synchronous collectives on older drivers.
Expose kernel-selection hints as advisory flags; actual kernel choice remains per-device local decision to avoid cross-machine lockstep.
Canary rollout for Dedicated clusters with a runtime feature flag; Private deployments will get opt-in until stability confirmed.
tradeoffs: Centralized controller simplifies global decisions but adds failure surface; mitigated by conservative defaults on controller loss.
Advisory hints improve flexibility but may lead to suboptimal local decisions if local telemetry is stale.
Aggressive NCCL overlap can increase GPU memory pressure due to concurrent buffers; need to balance with cache eviction policies.
blockers: Intermittent hangs observed on NCCL 2.16 with simultaneous collective + point-to-point traffic — requires vendor driver test or workaround.
Need kernel-selection telemetry to be low overhead; current instrumentation increased a hot-path allocation on some models.
performance_metrics: Baseline (4xA100, batch=8, mix of 16/512 tokens): p99 token latency = 420ms, NCCL overlap = 34%
Current prototype (4xA100): p99 token latency = 386ms, NCCL overlap = 43%
Target (8xA100, mixed): p99 token latency <= 360ms, NCCL overlap >= 55%
